Named violating input: a checkout with origin present but whose `git fetch` fails (e.g. unreachable remote) so referencing stays empty — the code must emit the freshness-specific refusal, not the missing-trailer refusal
advisory.finding: The new distinct 'checkout freshness' refusal branch is untested: when a remote is present (probe=='present') but the fetch fails or the remote refs stay invisible so referencing remains empty, close_precheck raises a specific CommandError declaring the failure 'distinct from a proven absence of a rebar-ticket trailer' — no test asserts this message or returncode, so a regression collapsing it back onto the ordinary missing-trailer refusal (or skipping the refresh) would go undetected.
scenarios: A stale server clone whose remote fetch fails; the gate must surface the freshness refusal so the agent retries with git fetch instead of being pushed toward --force
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches link_revert._remote_probe to return 'present' and link_revert._refresh_remote_refs to return False (or points origin at an unreachable/empty remote), sets file_impact with no local referencing commit, and asserts rebar.transition raises RebarError with returncode==1 and 'could not refresh or see its remote refs' in stderr.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] After a successful refresh+rescan that still finds no commit, fall through to the 'no commit references it' refusal rather than raising the freshness error, so a genuine absence is reported distinctly on repos with a remote.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:228: `if not referencing:` immediately raises the 'could not refresh or see its remote refs' error even when the refresh at line 219 returned True and the rescan ran cleanly
src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:236: `if own_impact and not referencing:` (the 'no commit references it' refusal) is only reached when probe == 'none' — so any repo with a remote never emits it

Ticket 0164-3ed8-45de-4330 AC: 'A refusal caused by the server being unable to SEE a commit is distinguishable in its message from a refusal caused by no commit referencing the ticket' and test step 2: 'Confirm a genuinely unreferenced ticket still refuses, with its own distinct message'
blocking.finding: After a SUCCESSFUL remote refresh and rescan that still finds no referencing commit (a genuine absence), the code raises the freshness/staleness CommandError instead of the ordinary 'no commit references it' refusal. For any checkout with a configured remote (probe != 'none'), the freshness message is always emitted and the specific missing-trailer message at line 236 becomes unreachable — inverting the very distinction the fix intends and the ticket AC requires.
blocking.suggested_fix: Only raise the freshness error when the refresh could NOT be performed/made refs visible (e.g. probe == 'unknown', or probe == 'present' and _refresh_remote_refs returned False). When the refresh succeeded and the rescan is still empty, do not raise here — let control fall through to the line 236 'no commit references it' refusal.
